subject: Re: EoQ surge: request for trial credit to close
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@edgeflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgeflow.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short trial top-up to secure EoQ commitment

Hi Ben / Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineers were impressed with the inference performance. We are very close to committing, but our procurement cycle runs through Friday and the CFO wants to see another week of usage before signing. Can Redwood provide a one-time 45k-token credit and extend the trial window by 30 days so we can validate throughput under our real traffic?

We can commit to a 12-month reserved plan if metrics look good; the immediate ask is just the top-up so we can complete procurement this week. I attached our last 7-day usage snapshot for reference.

Summary ask: 45,000 token credit, 30-day extension.

Appreciate a quick response — timing is tight.

Best,
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Engineering, EdgeFlow
samir@edgeflow.com

Attachment: usage_snapshot_20270512.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: short trial top-up to secure EoQ commitment

Irene — forwarding EdgeFlow's ask. Key points: they want 45k tokens + 30-day extension, and will likely convert to a 12-month reserved if throughput checks out. They said procurement needs the extended window to finish approvals by EoQ.

Proposed supplier-side terms (draft attached):
- One-time 45,000 token credit applied to account on approval
- Trial extended 30 days from credit activation
- Conversion condition: commit to 12-month reserved capacity within 30 days of extension and sign MSA addendum

Risk note: if they don't convert we absorb tokens; it's small relative to potential ARR but it's a precedent. Asking for approval to proceed and to confirm whether we can push this from sales authority or need finance sign-off.

If approved I will send a short DocuSign addendum to expedite.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: credit_terms_draft.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)

Ben — thanks for the context and draft. I’ll approve a one-time credit on the following conditions: 

1) Credit cap at 40,000 tokens (we reduce the ask slightly).
2) Customer must sign the MSA addendum and 12-month reserved commitment within 30 days of activation; if they don’t, remaining unused credit is forfeited and account is audited for anomalous usage.
3) Finance (Monica) must review the credit memo and mark it as "sales-approved exception" in our ledger.
4) CS to enable priority onboarding and a short performance checklist to minimize noise during evaluation.

Monica — please confirm you'll clear the accounting entry under the above structure. Marissa — can you coordinate CS for priority enablement and ensure we capture a simple acceptance metric (p95 latency and token-cost delta) so product has a clean evaluation?

Also log this in HubSpot (deal DL-2027-04567) and attach the signed addendum when complete. I am comfortable with 40k as a scalable play — the upside is meaningful.

I am cc’ing Samir to keep timelines transparent. I expect Ben to send the DocuSign link and credit activation instructions once Monica signs off.

-Irene
Irene Choi
VP, North America Sales, Redwood Inference
